title: The shallow-share rise was 9.59 points greater below M6.5 in filtered global M5.5+ ComCat records for 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether the change in shallow-earthquake share differs between separate magnitude groups in global ComCat records. We compared 2000-2012 with 2013-2025. After removal of exact depths of 10, 33 and 35 km, the share at depth <= 15 km rose by 10.87 percentage points for 5.5 <= M < 6.5 and by 1.28 points for M >= 6.5. The direct difference was 9.59 points. Its conditional 95% three-year block interval was 4.25 to 15.72 points. A fixed common-cell check gave 10.94 points, with an interval of 3.88 to 17.17. Threshold, shorter-period and moment-magnitude checks retained positive contrasts. This extends a prior nested comparison by testing the magnitude contrast directly with shared year resamples. The result describes a catalog pattern. It does not show physical shallowing or a cause. Revised depths, mixed magnitude methods, sequence clustering, broad geographic cells and only 26 years limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a retrieval recipe, an independent arithmetic audit and a figure are included. External source records remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Reported annual shallow shares and direct magnitude contrasts. Bars show conditional 95% three-year block intervals. Exact depth removal does not establish depth accuracy.

citations.reason: Same source CSV, eras, depth filter and cutoff. We test a direct contrast between separate magnitude groups. No source code was reused.
